pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher’s Message | Castle Hill Primary School
pageCache.text:
Castle Hill Primary School
Headteacher’s Message
Welcome to Castle Hill Primary School
Our school is a thriving community where relationships are key and children are enthusiastic about their learning.
We were delighted that our latest OFSTED inspection in April 2025 recognised this, stating:
‘The school has a calm and purposeful atmosphere. Pupils behave exceptionally well. They listen wellto adults and their peers. Across the school, pupils demonstrate highly positive attitudes to learning.They enjoy school and are keen to learn. The school has high expectations for its pupils.'
Our mantra is that ‘Words matter. Why?’
Language development is vital to a child’s future success. We need words to communicate our ideas, express our feelings and connect with others.
From the very beginning of a child’s school journey with us, we focus on developing vocabulary and understanding of language. This is central to our bespoke curriculum which is designed to effectively build skills and knowledge across all subjects from Reception to Year 6.
Our key drivers are ‘Curiosity, Bravery, Belonging, Pride and Integrity.’
We encourage all our pupils to be curious about their learning and the world around them; to take on challenges and to stand up for what is right; to help all members of our school community to feel like they truly belong; to be proud of themselves and their achievements and to act with integrity.
I am privileged to lead this wonderful school and I look forward to welcoming you.
Mrs. Karen EttrickHeadteacher
Castle Hill Primary School

pageCache.pageTitle: VIPERS and Vocabulary | Castle Hill Primary School
pageCache.text:
Castle Hill Primary School
VIPERS and Vocabulary
Vocabulary is at the heart of our curriculum. Research has shown that pupils need to understand 98% of the words they read to understand what they are reading. Every class has a focus 'Word of the Week' which children are taught to use in context. They are also exposed to, and explicitly taught, a rich range of vocabulary through reading and the wider curriculum. All classes use a multi-sensory approach to VIPERS (Rob Smith - The Literacy Shed) to aid the teaching of comprehension skills.
Castle Hill Primary School

pageCache.pageTitle: Breakfast Club / The Keep | Castle Hill Primary School
pageCache.text:
Castle Hill Primary School
The Keep After School Club
The Keep is a happy, fun, reliable and, most importantly, safe out-of-school care provision for pupils of Castle Hill Primary School.
The club runs on site daily during term time from 3:15 pm–5:15 pm by staff who are also employed by the school. This means your child has familiar faces to greet them at the end of their busy school day!
The Keep is owned and managed by Katie Ward, who is also employed by Castle Hill and has over 20 years of childcare experience.
CLICK HERE thekeep.kidsclubhq.co.uk TO REGISTER AND BOOK THE KEEP!
Email: thekeep@virginmedia.com for more information or queries
Castle Hill Primary School

pageCache.pageTitle: A Reading Day in KS2 | Castle Hill Primary School
pageCache.text:
Castle Hill Primary School
A Reading Day in KS2
Reading in KS2
“The most successful learning occurs when children are guided by adults towards learning things that they could not attempt to learn on their own.” (Vgotsky)
As pupils enter KS2, we recognise how important it is that they continue to develop their reading fluency alongside developing their comprehension skills and love of reading.
Pupils continue to embed their phonics skills as they enter Y3. All classes are taught using a whole class reading approach ensuring that every child has access to high quality texts and high quality first teaching from a reading expert.
These whole class reading sessions are taught 3 - 4 x per week and texts are selected carefully across the Key Stage 2 classes. These sessions combine a balance of teacher modelling reading with prosody and fluency, echo, paired or choral reading, pre-teaching or discovery of new vocabulary and, where applicable, pre-teaching of the social/cultural/historical/geographical context of the book.
All classes use a multi-sensory approach to VIPERS (an acronym for the 6 reading domains of the National Curriculum created by Rob Smith – The Literacy Shed) to aid the teaching of comprehension skills. Whole class reading sessions across the course of a week include: high quality paired and whole class discussion around the text, teacher modelled answers and both verbal and written responses.
Pupils are also heard read individually as often as possible by the teacher, teaching assistants or trained parent/grandparent helpers or other trained volunteers.
In addition, pupils have a wide range of opportunities to read in other areas of the curriculum as well as being read to every day.
Older pupils pair up with younger pupils to become reading buddies and they have access to a variety of quality fiction and non-fiction through class book corners and the use of both the Community Reading Hub and the KS2 library.
Castle Hill Primary School

pageCache.pageTitle: Reading Aloud | Castle Hill Primary School
pageCache.text:
Castle Hill Primary School
Reading Aloud
We continue to develop pupils' reading fluency across KS2 through providing many opportunities for children to read aloud. During reading lessons, teachers incorporate a variety of methods such as paired reading, choral reading and echo reading. Children are also given opportunities to read aloud in the wider curriculum for example: reciting poems; reading poems aloud and accompanying them with musical instruments; reading stories to younger children; reading aloud in assemblies; presenting work in class as well as role play and drama opportunities.
Castle Hill Primary School

pageCache.pageTitle: Bedtime Stories | Castle Hill Primary School
pageCache.text:
Castle Hill Primary School
Bedtime Stories
A successful event is when the parents are invited in with their children. This is evident in our annual 'Bedtime stories' events which were introduced in 2020. Both parents and children are invited to come to school in their pyjamas and snuggle up with their teddies whilst listening to stories read by their teachers. They then snuggle up with their parents and choose from a selection of books from a range of genres to enjoy a cosy storytime session together.
